summary: Right-handed basketball layup at takeoff: pushing off the left foot, right knee driven up to hip height, ball carried in both hands up past the right shoulder.

environment.text: Rim 3.05 m high, {fwd:rim:pelvis} cm ahead and above; backboard square behind the rim.

cameras.name: baseline_low
cameras.text: From under the basket looking up, knee drive and ball carry clear.

cameras.name: side
cameras.text: Profile: takeoff foot pushing off, thigh horizontal.

cameras.name: wide_cinema
cameras.text: Wide from the wing, defenders blurred, rim in the upper frame.

rules.why: shooting-side knee driven up, thigh about horizontal
takeoff leg nearly straight at toe-off
left foot still pushing off the floor (right-handed layup takes off from the left foot)

text.action: a basketball player taking off for a right-handed layup
text.core: Pushing off the left foot on the ball of the foot, left leg nearly straight; right knee driven up to hip height, thigh horizontal, knee bent about 90 degrees; trunk upright; ball held in both hands and carried up past the right shoulder toward head height, right hand under the ball, left hand on its side.
text.gaze: Eyes on the top corner of the square on the backboard.
cues: right-handed layup: take off from the left foot
protect the ball with two hands up to the shoulder
kinetic: sneaker sole flexing on the push-off
shorts lifted by the knee drive
motion blur on the trailing arm swing, sharp face
avoid: ball held low in one hand
both feet off the floor with no push-off

sources.cite: FIBA WABC Level 1 manual 2.7.2: right-handed layup takes off from the left foot, lift the shooting-hand-side knee
Vint & Hinrichs 1996, J Appl Biomech: one-foot jumps gain height from the free-leg swing
